AI models and their tools — Claude Code among them — are moving fast, and many of us are still figuring out how to use them productively in research. Practices are far from settled: shifting from chat interfaces to agents that act on our machines; managing context, permissions, and subscription limits; citing AI assistance in papers; choosing the right model for mathematics, coding, or sensitive data; and deciding what to automate versus what still needs careful human judgment.

This 2026-2027 cycle accompanies the Claude Code licences offered to CREST members. It provides **short 1h30 trainings**, held in person and online, and recorded, to get started with the tool, show concrete uses and their limits, and exchange on how they change our work.

Organizers: Nicolas Brosse, Émilien Schultz. Questions and ideas: [Discussions](https://github.com/orgs/crest-science/discussions).
